outcome_definition: Recorded criminal offence rate per 100,000 residents by statistical area (SA2/LGA) and year, from NSW Police / NSW Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research (SBS) open data.
notes: Curated seed catalog grounded in Australian criminological literature. Used as the fallback when the local LLM is unavailable, and as the seed that LLM discovery merges with. Individual-level offender attributes (age, gender, education of offenders) are NOT available in NSW open data; area-level proxies are used instead and results are interpreted at the area level.

factors.name: Unemployment rate
factors.definition: Share of the labour force aged 15+ that is unemployed and actively seeking work.

proxies.variable: Persons labour force status - unemployment rate

citations: Nelson, M. (2002) 'Crime, unemployment and youth: a panel study for Australia', Applied Economics
factors.notes: causes: reduced legitimate income and informal social control; also a strong confounder for area disadvantage.

factors.name: Median household income
factors.definition: Median weekly household income of occupied private dwellings.
citations: Trickett, P. & Adolphe, A. (2020) 'The geography of recorded crime in Australia', AIC Trends & Issues 548
factors.notes: confounder: common cause of many other factors; absolute vs relative deprivation debate.

factors.name: Income inequality
factors.definition: Within-area dispersion of household income (e.g. 80/20 ratio or Gini).
citations: Weatherburn, D. (2015) 'The Economics of Crime in Australia', Australia & Society Series

factors.name: Year 12 or equivalent completion
factors.definition: Share of people aged 20-64 who completed Year 12 or equivalent.
citations: Carrington, J. (2020) 'Crime and justice trends in Australia', AIC
factors.notes: area-level proxy for the unavailable individual offender education attribute; human-capital mechanism.

factors.name: Youth population share
factors.definition: Share of residents aged 15-24 (the peak offending age band).
citations: Donnelly, N., Scott, J. & Poynton, S. (2017) 'Geographic trends in robbery in NSW', AIC Trends & Issues 525
factors.notes: age structure is the single strongest demographic confounder of area crime rates; area-level proxy for offender age.

factors.name: Lone-parent households
factors.definition: Share of families with children that are one-parent families.
citations: Weatherburn, D. (2015) 'The Economics of Crime in Australia'
factors.notes: social-disorganisation mechanism; highly confounded by income; risk of stigmatising interpretation - handle with care.

factors.name: Dwelling crowding
factors.definition: Share of occupied private dwellings with one or more extra bedroom needed (crowding index).
citations: Moore, T., Adolphe, A. & Kavanagh, A. (2021) 'Crime prevention through urban design and place management', Crime Prevention Science
factors.notes: mediator between poverty and crime; routine-activity mechanism.

factors.name: Rent burden (housing stress)
factors.definition: Share of renting households paying more than 30% of household income on rent.

proxies.variable: Rent as a percentage of household income

citations: Moore, T., Adolphe, A. & Kavanagh, A. (2021) op. cit.
factors.notes: financial-stress mechanism; mediator between income shocks and offending.

factors.name: Rental vacancy shortage
factors.definition: Annual rental vacancy rate (inverted: shortage = low vacancy).

proxies.dataset: NSW Tenant Fee and Rental Commission - Rental Market Reports

citations: Moore, T. et al. (2021) op. cit.
factors.notes: housing-market tightness as driver of crowding and mobility.

factors.name: Public housing concentration
factors.definition: Share of occupied dwellings rented from state/territory housing authorities.

proxies.variable: Dwelling tenure - rented from State or Territory Housing Authority

factors.notes: concentration-of-disadvantage mechanism; strongly confounded by income and public-housing allocation policy.

factors.name: Public transport access
factors.definition: Share of dwellings within walking distance of frequent public transport (or Transport Access score).

proxies.dataset: NSW Transport for NSW - Transport for NSW Access Panel / open data

citations: Moore, T. et al. (2021) op. cit.
factors.notes: access to legitimate activity spaces; also raises guardianship/target flux - ambiguous sign.

factors.name: Alcohol outlet density
factors.definition: Licensed on-premises and packaged liquor outlets per 1,000 residents.

proxies.dataset: Liquor & Gaming NSW - licensed premises register

citations: Kavanagh, A. & Virgil, H. (2017) 'The theoretical underpinnings of alcohol-related harm and proposals for policy change', Int. J. Drug Policy
factors.notes: routine activity: convergence of motivated offenders and suitable targets around venues; disinhibiting effect of alcohol.

factors.name: Gambling venue density
factors.definition: Registered clubs and venues with gaming machines per 1,000 residents.

proxies.dataset: Liquor & Gaming NSW / Independent Liquor & Gaming Authority registers
proxies.variable: count of registered clubs with gaming machines

factors.notes: financial stress from problem gambling; property-crime mechanism.

factors.name: Ambulatory mental-health separations
factors.definition: Mental-health related ambulatory care sensitive conditions separations per 1,000 (PHN/HHN level).

proxies.dataset: AIHW / NSW Health - Ambulatory Care Sensitive Conditions

citations: AIHW (2023) 'Alcohol, tobacco & other drugs in Australia'
factors.notes: bidirectional with offending; use lagged values.

factors.name: SEIFA relative disadvantage
factors.definition: ABS SEIFA Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage (IRSD) score for the area.

proxies.variable: SEIFA Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage

citations: Johnson, M. (2018) 'Using SEIFA and its associated indices when working with disadvantaged areas', ABS Views
factors.notes: composite confounder; preferred over ethnicity-based proxies for ethical governance reasons.

factors.name: Transient / visitor population
factors.definition: Visitors present on Census night plus unoccupied dwellings share - proxy for population flux (tourism, FIFO, construction workforce).

proxies.variable: Number of visitors on Census night; Unoccupied private dwellings

citations: Trickett, P. & Adolphe, A. (2020) op. cit.
factors.notes: routine activity: targets and motivated strangers converge; also inflates denominator of per-capita rates.

factors.name: Hot days
factors.definition: Annual count of days at or above 35 degrees C at the nearest BOM station.

proxies.dataset: Bureau of Meteorology - Climate data online

citations: Currey, R. C. (1973) 'Air temperature and violent crime', Sociological Inquiry
factors.notes: heat-aggression and routine-activity mechanisms; strongest for violent crime.

factors.name: Police resourcing
factors.definition: Police officers per 100,000 residents by Local Area Command.

proxies.dataset: NSW Police Force open data / annual reports

citations: Weatherburn, D. & Vignaendra, S. (2003) 'Does increased police presence reduce crime?', NSW SBS Technical Paper 3
factors.notes: simultaneity: police are deployed to high-crime areas (reverse causation); use lags and instrument where possible.
